# Backeer for OpenCode

`backeer-opencode` connects OpenCode to Backeer. It sends mobile notifications
for permission requests, questions, completed todo lists, completed assistant
runs, session failures, prolonged retries, and OpenCode updates. While a
permission or question is pending, it also consumes an authenticated Backeer
command stream. An authorized user can choose **Allow once**, **Always allow**,
or **Reject** for permissions and can answer or reject AI questions from the
Backeer iOS application.

Mobile notifications and approvals use outbound HTTPS only. The optional live
control feature adds an authenticated loopback-only listener inside OpenCode;
it needs no public port, inbound firewall rule, or separately hosted server.
See [Live control setup](docs/live-control.md) for the SSE/MCP connection.

With live control configured, the listener remains ready for the lifetime of
the owning OpenCode process, including when no Codex chat is connected. Failed
binds and unexpected listener closure retry on the same loopback port every
three seconds. OpenCode shutdown stops the listener and retries.

OpenCode V2's native footer shows **Backeer · Bağlantı bekleniyor**, **Codex bağlı**,
or the configuration/recovery state. A connection to another session is shown
separately. Status uses native RPC events; it adds no prompts or model calls.
The legacy server-only side-loaded bundle cannot display a TUI footer.

In legacy single-project mode, **Backeer · Klasör eşleşmiyor** (formerly “Diğer proje”) means the configured `liveBridge.projectDirectory`
differs from the current OpenCode working directory after path normalization.
The listener stays inactive in this location; the label does not establish a
connection to another project. A different subfolder or worktree also counts as
a different location. This is separate from **Codex diğer oturumda**, which
describes an existing connection associated with another session.

## Reliability and local storage (0.16.0)

Notification events, acknowledgement receipts and question state updates use a
protected disk outbox with one active send per native notification owner. Network
errors, 429 and 5xx responses retry every three seconds; restarting OpenCode resumes
pending jobs automatically. A queued receipt means saved locally, not delivered.
Permanent failures are retained as `failed-*.json` for inspection and reported.
Actionable question creation still waits for the gateway's actual event ID and is
cancelled when the native form settles. No per-event infinite retry workers are
created for ordinary notifications.

The default queue is `~/.config/opencode/notification-outbox` (or under
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`). Set `notificationQueueDirectory` or
`BACKEER_OUTBOX_DIRECTORY` to another private writable directory if needed.
Directories/files use owner-only permissions and contain complete event payloads,
so protect this directory like local conversation history. Authorization headers
and source token values are not stored in jobs. Queues are isolated by endpoint,
project and source credential; changing credentials does not send the prior
source's backlog using the new token. Restore that source to resume its queue.
Retained jobs consume disk until delivered or manually reviewed.

The command journal reads historical receipts lazily and caches at most 256 records
in RAM. Durable journals retain exact old request IDs and native question guards;
no age/count expiration makes an uncertain write eligible for replay. Unconfigured
non-durable journals use a private process-lifetime temporary spool, removed on
normal disposal. Mobile **control** SSE rejects a frame above 1 MiB, an incomplete
frame after ten seconds, or no heartbeat after 45 seconds and releases its reader.
Live assistant/tool output uses its separate existing retention budgets.

## Automatic file and directory approvals

From 0.12.0, file and directory access prompts are answered automatically with
OpenCode's native **Always allow** decision. This is enabled whenever the plugin
is loaded, including when mobile notifications are disabled or no Backeer ingest
token is configured. It applies to the exact permission actions `read`, `edit`,
`glob`, `grep`, `list` (V1), and `external_directory`. OpenCode's `edit` permission
covers file writes and patches as well.

The plugin replies to the existing request with `always`; it does not rewrite
permission configuration. OpenCode determines the saved patterns and their
lifetime. In V2, these are durable project-scoped approvals and configured deny
rules remain enforced. See [OpenCode permissions](https://dev.opencode.ai/v2/docs/permissions/#approvals).
An external-directory approval grants the directory boundary; a separate shell
permission still follows the normal approval flow. Shell commands, web access,
subagent launches, authentication and unknown permission types are not included.

Successful automatic replies do not create a second mobile approval card.
Duplicate request events share one native reply. If the native reply cannot be
applied, the existing native/mobile flow remains available; no success is claimed.

## Live output and instructions

The opt-in live channel lets a local MCP client send an instruction to an exact
OpenCode session and follow assistant text, tool results, status and pending
approval metadata over SSE. It does not record the whole terminal, export
reasoning or authentication forms, or approve permissions. Mobile approval and
question replies continue through Backeer as before.

In managed mode, `select_session` reads the chosen connection's current sessions
and asks the user which one to follow. Hosts supporting MCP form elicitation
show a native selection form. Other hosts receive a structured `choose_session`
result so the assistant can present the choices using its own question UI.
Selection returns the exact session ID without opening a binding. After the
user chooses, `connect_session` attaches this chat to that ID and automatically
follows its subagents. Session titles are labels, not an instruction to choose
a target; duplicate titles are distinguished by their IDs. See
[interactive session selection](docs/live-control.md#interactive-session-selection-0120).

Create a separate protected live-control credential file on the OpenCode host;
use the same credential in an owner-only file on the MCP computer. Do not reuse
the Backeer ingest token. Values never belong in plugin options or chat text.
For example, generate a file without printing its contents:

```sh
install -d -m 700 "$HOME/.config/opencode/secrets"
(set -C; umask 077; openssl rand -hex 32 > "$HOME/.config/opencode/secrets/backeer-live-token")
```

This refuses to overwrite an existing live-control file; generate it once for
initial setup, not during a running session. Enable the plugin with non-secret
options (use an actual absolute path):

```json
{
  "plugins": [{
    "package": "backeer-opencode",
    "options": {
      "liveBridge": {
        "enabled": true,
        "port": 43871,
        "tokenFile": "/absolute/private/path/backeer-live-token"
      }
    }
  }]
}
```

For side-loaded installations, the equivalent environment variables are
`BACKEER_LIVE_ENABLED=true`, `BACKEER_LIVE_PORT=43871`, and
`BACKEER_LIVE_TOKEN_FILE=/absolute/private/path/backeer-live-token`. Defaults:
disabled; port `43871`; token file under the existing OpenCode configuration
directory at `secrets/backeer-live-token`. An invalid live configuration disables
only the live channel, leaving existing mobile integration available. Restart
the intended OpenCode process after explicitly installing/enabling this version;
existing running sessions are not modified by this source checkout.

The matching `backeer-opencode-mcp` executable is provided in the package.
Connect through an existing SSH tunnel and register the local stdio executable
as described in [the complete setup guide](docs/live-control.md). Version 0.6.0
in this checkout must be installed from its built package or installer bundle
until it has been separately published; do not assume npm `latest` contains it.

Version 0.6.0 also supports saved connections and separate per-chat session
bindings. Set `BACKEER_LIVE_PROFILES_FILE` on the local MCP adapter, or use the
bundled connection tools in `backeer-codex` 0.3.0. Existing `BACKEER_LIVE_URL` /
`BACKEER_LIVE_TOKEN_FILE` single-connection configuration still exposes its
original tools, plus ordinary question reading/answering in 0.8.0. See [per-chat connections](docs/live-control.md#per-chat-connections).

## Requirements

- OpenCode V2 (tested against 2.0.26), or V1 1.18.29 and newer
- Node.js 18 or newer for the local installer and tests
- Outbound HTTPS access to `external-gateway.backeer.com:443` for mobile integration
- A Backeer source ingest token for mobile notifications and remote answers

Create a separate Backeer source and ingest token for every server. Sharing a
token causes permission commands to be broadcast to every OpenCode process that
uses that token and weakens host-level auditing and revocation.

## Local installation

The local installer copies a single self-contained plugin file into OpenCode's
global plugin directory. OpenCode discovers it automatically.

```sh
cd opencode-plugin
node bin/backeer-opencode.js --token-file /path/from/your/secret-manager/backeer-token
```

The resulting files are:

```text
~/.config/opencode/plugins/backeer-permission.js
~/.config/opencode/secrets/backeer-ingest-token
```

The token file is written with mode `0600`. When `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, the
installer and plugin use `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` instead. To update only the
plugin while preserving the existing token, run:

```sh
node bin/backeer-opencode.js
```

Restart OpenCode after installation or update.

## Installation from npm

Install the package in OpenCode's global configuration:

```sh
opencode plugin add backeer-opencode
npx backeer-opencode@latest configure
```

`configure` asks for the source ingest token without echoing it, stores it with
mode `0600`, and does not install a second side-loaded plugin. If a token already
exists, replacement requires confirmation.

Alternatively, add it to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` manually:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["backeer-opencode"]
}
```

OpenCode installs configured npm plugins automatically. Restart OpenCode after
installation. The npm package never contains a token; provide the token using
one of the methods below.

If npm package loading is not available in a particular OpenCode installation,
install the package as a side-loaded plugin instead:

```sh
npx backeer-opencode@latest install \
  --token-file /path/from/your/secret-manager/backeer-token
```

Use either the configured npm plugin or the side-loaded form, not both. Loading
both forms would register the integration twice.

## Authentication

The plugin checks these locations in order:

1. `BACKEER_INGEST_TOKEN`
2. `BACKEER_TOKEN_FILE`
3. `~/.config/opencode/secrets/backeer-ingest-token`

Do not commit the token to an OpenCode configuration file, shell script, plugin
file, or repository. Do not reuse an application-session token; this plugin
requires a source ingest token.

## Configuration

The default gateway origin is `https://external-gateway.backeer.com`. These
environment variables are supported:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `BACKEER_INGEST_TOKEN` | Source credential; takes precedence over a token file |
| `BACKEER_TOKEN_FILE` | Absolute path to a protected token file |
| `BACKEER_ORIGIN` | Gateway origin; HTTPS is required |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_PERMISSIONS` | Set to `false` to disable permission notifications and remote replies |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_QUESTIONS` | Set to `false` to disable question notifications and remote answers |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_TODOS` | Set to `false` to disable todo-completion notifications |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_LIFECYCLE` | Set to `false` to disable every lifecycle notification |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_SESSION_COMPLETED` | Set to `false` to disable successful-run notifications |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_SESSION_ERRORS` | Set to `false` to disable session-error notifications |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_SESSION_RETRIES` | Set to `false` to disable retry warnings |
| `BACKEER_NOTIFY_OPENCODE_UPDATES` | Set to `false` to disable OpenCode update notifications |
| `BACKEER_SESSION_COMPLETION_MIN_SECONDS` | Minimum run duration; defaults to `0` (every completion) |
| `BACKEER_RETRY_ATTEMPT_THRESHOLD` | First retry attempt that triggers a warning; defaults to `3` |
| `BACKEER_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` (default), `error`, `debug`, or `silent` |

For npm installations, non-secret options can also be supplied through the
OpenCode V2 plugin options syntax:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "backeer-opencode",
      "options": {
        "permissions": true,
        "questions": true,
        "todos": true,
        "lifecycle": {
          "enabled": true,
          "completed": true,
          "errors": true,
          "retries": true,
          "updates": true,
          "completionMinSeconds": 0,
          "retryAttemptThreshold": 3
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Supported options are `origin`, `tokenFile`, `permissions`, `questions`,
`todos`, `lifecycle`, `liveBridge`, and `logLevel`. Use `"lifecycle": false` to disable the
entire lifecycle group. The token itself is deliberately not a plugin option.

## Conversation feedback

On OpenCode V1, user-facing status messages appear as compact Backeer entries in the OpenCode
conversation:

```text
Backeer ✓ Permission request sent
Backeer ✓ Question sent
Backeer ✓ Todo completion sent
Backeer ✓ Task completion sent
Backeer ✓ Decision applied: Always allow
```

These entries are marked `noReply` and `ignored`, so they are visible without
starting another agent turn or entering model context. Feedback generated while
an agent is active, a permission prompt is open, or a question is awaiting an
answer remains queued until the interaction closes and the session becomes idle.
It never writes to the user's input field or replaces interactive OpenCode UI.

On V2, automatic delivery feedback stays in server logs: the V1 ignored/noReply
conversation API no longer exists. `/backeer` command results use a synthetic
entry with `resume: false`, so they do not start an agent turn, but they can be
included in later model context. No credentials are displayed.

Technical diagnostics use V1's structured application log API or V2's captured
server stderr, never stdout. Normal `info` logging omits HTTP details; set
`BACKEER_LOG_LEVEL=debug` when technical details are needed. Set it to `error`
for failures only or `silent` to disable structured logs.

## OpenCode command

The plugin registers a `/backeer` command inside OpenCode:

```text
/backeer
/backeer status
/backeer doctor
/backeer test
/backeer update-check
/backeer update
/backeer token
/backeer token-file /absolute/path/to/a/protected-token-file
```

The status report shows the plugin version, gateway reachability, token source,
notification switches and lifecycle thresholds, command-stream state, pending
permissions, and log level. It never displays the token. Gateway reachability
does not validate the source credential.

`/backeer doctor` performs a read-only diagnostic pass. It verifies the local
configuration, protected token-file permissions, source authentication, event
and command capabilities, and gateway APNs readiness. It does not create an
event, open a command stream, or display the bearer token.

`/backeer test` publishes one uniquely correlated, non-actionable application
event and asks the gateway to deliver a real push notification. Use it after
installation, token rotation, or network changes to verify the complete path
from OpenCode to the phone.

`/backeer token` displays safe rotation instructions. Never paste a raw token
into slash-command arguments because OpenCode may retain command text in session
history. To rotate from inside OpenCode, first place the new token in an absolute
file readable only by its owner (`chmod 600`), then use `token-file`. The plugin
atomically copies it to the configured token location, applies mode `0600`, and
activates it immediately without restarting OpenCode. The source file is not
removed.

In shared mode, sessions created directly in real Git worktrees are included
automatically after verifying their actual Git common directory on the owner.
This survives plugin reload without storing session IDs in configuration. The
session picker labels the worktree when available. Separate Git repositories
still require their own project connection. A native API outage is reported as
`native_session_api_unavailable`, verified foreign scope as
`session_project_mismatch`, archived rows as `session_archived`, and absence in
the selected native owner as `session_unavailable`. None proves deletion from
another owner or project. Multiple owners of one project merge their inventories;
an exact session is routed to its verified native API and observed event owner.

## Compact activity and on-demand details (0.14.0)

`watch_activity` is the default managed MCP follow tool. `activity_status` returns
one compact root/agent view with counts, coverage and verified completion.
Ordinary changes coalesce for 500 ms by default; questions, permissions and errors
wake the tool immediately. Completion requires a fresh complete tree snapshot:
an idle parent cannot complete a busy child. Pending native status requests do
not hold urgent alerts. Optional MCP progress messages carry short status text
when the host requests them; continuous UI rendering depends on the host.

Full output stays in bounded retained history. `read_details` lists references
using independent detail cursors; pass an eventId and offset/maxChars to page its
text. Reading details or the compact card does not consume `read_events`.
Expiry/interruption is explicit, never a fabricated summary or silent skip.
Use `activity_metrics` for received bytes, returned tool-response UTF-8 bytes,
cache hits and retained/evicted events. These are not billed model token counts.
No additional summarization model or full-log prompt is needed.

Shared mode now reads all native owners in the same verified Git project,
including distinct worktrees; exact parentID ancestry still excludes unrelated
sessions. The old single-owner SSE proxy could miss direct child output even
though parent summaries arrived. Protocol v2 uses one canonical replay stream
and resolves ancestry across owners. Reload all old gateway owner processes
when upgrading; a v1 listener on the same port cannot supply this protocol.
The local Codex adapter must also be updated (0.11.0+). An old remote bridge
must be updated and loaded before the new activity tools can be used.

This covers native OpenCode child sessions. Agents running opaquely inside a
separate Codex process require that process to expose its own agent events;
they cannot be reconstructed from the OpenCode parent's final text.

## Follow-up delivery (0.14.1)

V2 live-control instructions now use native `delivery: "steer"` with `resume: true`.
Earlier versions forced `queue`, which leaves follow-ups pending until the
session reaches an idle boundary. A steer becomes available at the next safe
step boundary while the current task is running; an idle runner is woken.
Admission (`accepted`) is not proof of delivery or execution: a running tool,
provider response, permission prompt or question can still delay processing.
Existing queued inputs are unchanged. Changing delivery mode does not resend
old messages or grant permission to duplicate them. Native admission/delivery
semantics: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/specs/v2/session.md

## Slow native APIs (0.14.2)

Health checks have a 3-second budget; native-owner session reads have 10 seconds.
The public gateway allows 30 seconds for an aggregated snapshot, and the updated
client allows 45 seconds for HTTP requests and SSE handshakes. The reconnect
interval remains 3 seconds and is independent of the handshake/read deadline.
An explicit caller-selected verification deadline still takes precedence;
`verify_connection` defaults to 30 seconds per check.

Inventory/tree verification uses at most eight concurrent reads per inventory
pass, preserves list order and exact ownership, and shares concurrent in-flight
native lists without caching stale results. Health liveness does not wait for
inventory recovery. This fixes healthy inventories that previously exceeded
the gateway's 1.5-second deadline and were reported as unavailable.

A read deadline now returns HTTP 504 with `native_session_api_timeout`;
HTTP 503 `native_session_api_unavailable` still describes an unreachable or
unverified native source. Neither proves session deletion. Keep the selected
binding and retry reads after recovery; never blindly resend a command.
Update the remote bridge to 0.14.2 and the local Codex adapter to 0.11.1 to get
the longer budgets throughout the path. Existing running owners need to load
the new code; updating only the local client cannot extend a remote deadline.

## Reliability and direct tools (0.15.0)

- Activity is projected from authenticated SSE, with fresh native reconciliation
  on membership/reconnect/terminal uncertainty and a 30-second periodic check.
  changesOnly:true returns deltas after the first card, without another model.
- Native V2 inbox events provide queued/delivered/cancelled receipts. GET
  /v1/sessions/:session/instructions/:request reads the exact persisted receipt.
  Accepted means admission. Session execution is not per-instruction completion.
- Protected command journals reserve request IDs before admission and preserve
  signatures/receipts across restarts. Prompts/answers/credentials are not stored.
  Interrupted reservations fail closed; no automatic POST replay. Guarantees
  begin with requests recorded by 0.15.0, not historical requests. Do not delete
  journals to repair uncertainty. Shared owners of one verified Git project use
  one journal directory next to their protected registry.
- MCP connection_report separates adapter/embedded/loaded remote versions,
  feature compatibility, owner circuits and latency; unknown checks remain
  unknown. backeer-opencode status displays native RPC state without a model.
  With the TUI entry loaded, /backeer-status or the “Backeer: Bağlantı raporu”
  palette command displays the same local report. keymap registration is owned
  by an app slot so it runs within the native UI context.
- Compatible bindings in one MCP manager share one SSE per authenticated
  endpoint/project; independent cursors, scoped buffers and gap acknowledgement
  remain per binding. Separate MCP processes keep separate transports.
- tail_output, read_errors and tool_result fetch retained source text on demand
  with explicit clipping/expiry. They never consume raw/detail cursors.
- list_questions/answer_question accept an explicit targetSessionId for an
  ordinary descendant form; client and server verify ancestry freshly and pin
  native form revision. Instructions remain root-only. Permission/authentication
  forms are excluded; existing native filesystem auto-allow remains unchanged.
- Health metadata advertises liveProtocol major 1 and optional capabilities.
  Incompatible majors block tracking and commands; missing optional features
  are not inferred from a version string. Old owners must be reloaded for all
  new features; local npm installation does not update remote processes.
- Three consecutive native read failures open a per-owner circuit for ten
  seconds with a single recovery probe. Writes are never retried by this circuit.
  Existing 3/10/30/45-second health/native/aggregate/client budgets remain.

Journals use owner-only directories/files on POSIX and fsync reservations and
immutable transition markers. Unreadable/corrupt reservations remain blocked.
Keep these records when reloading or upgrading the bridge. Receipt lookups are
scoped by project/session/request. A missing receipt is not evidence of no send.
Native V1 transports can expose unknown delivery. Output retention is bounded;
these tools cannot reconstruct expired history or opaque provider-side agents.

## 0.16.0 — 2026-11-06

- Dispose project hubs/listeners after the last native owner and reader leave, while preserving watched streams through owner outages.
- Store notification retries in a protected, restartable disk outbox with one worker per owner, cancellable retries and stable event identities. Queue admission is distinguished from actual delivery; permanent failures remain inspectable.
- Bound mobile control SSE frames (1 MiB, 10-second partial-frame and 45-second heartbeat deadlines), cancel stalled readers and release their locks.
- Replace unbounded in-memory command history with a lazy disk journal and 256-record cache. Preserve historical IDs, delivery indexes and native question reservations across eviction/restart without retaining prompts or answers.
- Retry transient automatic filesystem permission failures on a subsequent exact request event; keep native ownership, successful-decision deduplication and manual fallback.

## 0.15.1 — 2026-11-06

- Omit absent optional owner/mode diagnostic fields so the native OpenCode RPC JSON-value encoder accepts reports in disabled or unconfigured locations.
- Add a regression check for native JSON round-trip validity. No changes to the live wire protocol or Codex adapter compatibility.

## 0.15.0 — 2026-11-06

- Project session state from SSE with event-triggered/periodic reconciliation and optional compact deltas.
- Persist exact request reservations and receipts across restarts; track V2 native inbox delivery separately from session execution. Never replay uncertain commands automatically.
- Share authenticated SSE within each MCP manager while keeping binding scope, cursors and gaps independent.
- Add connection_report, instruction_status, tail_output, read_errors and tool_result (25 managed tools), plus native RPC/CLI/TUI diagnostics without synthetic model messages.
- Answer ordinary descendant questions from the existing binding after fresh client/server ancestry and native revision checks.
- Negotiate protocol/capabilities and report loaded versions separately; cool down repeated native read failures with one recovery probe, without retrying writes.

## 0.14.2 — 2026-11-06

- Separate health checks (3 seconds), individual native-owner reads (10 seconds), aggregated snapshots (30 seconds), and client HTTP/handshakes (45 seconds). Discovery and SSE handshakes no longer reuse the 3-second reconnect interval as a query deadline.
- Verify native inventory and tree members in batches of up to eight reads, preserving native list order, exact ownership and Git/worktree scope. Concurrent native inventory requests share only in-flight work; subsequent reads remain fresh.
- Expire stalled native read waiters so later reads can recover; mark temporarily unverified inventories partial instead of claiming sessions disappeared.
- Return a distinct retryable `native_session_api_timeout` (HTTP 504) on an actual native read deadline instead of conflating slow reads with unavailable APIs (503). Keep health liveness independent of inventory resynchronization.
- Preserve exact root command routing, request-ID deduplication and no automatic POST retries. Update the bundled Codex adapter to 0.11.1 for coordinated client time budgets and diagnostics.

## 0.14.1 — 2026-11-04

- Send V2 live-control instructions as native `steer` input with `resume: true`, instead of forcing every message into `queue`. Busy sessions can deliver follow-ups at their next safe step boundary; idle sessions are explicitly woken.
- Preserve root targeting and request-ID deduplication. This does not bypass a pending permission/question or interrupt running tools, and does not replay/promote existing queued messages.

## 0.14.0 — 2026-11-04

- Fan in live output from every native owner of a verified Git project, including worktrees and late/nested child sessions. Resolve parent ancestry across owners and keep one canonical replay cursor. Continue routing writes only to the selected root's owning native API.
- Add deterministic activity_status/watch_activity views, coalesced ordinary updates, immediate question/permission/error alerts, and tree-verified completion. No extra model is used for summaries.
- Add read_details with separate per-source cursors and text paging, plus activity_metrics with measured UTF-8 response bytes and cache/retention counters (not billed model tokens).
- Cache read-only activity/detail verification for at most one second; invalidate on stream generation, events, gaps and writes. Commands and answers always verify freshly.
- Mark native upstream interruptions and gateway restarts as explicit history gaps. Internal fan-in readers do not appear as connected Codex users or produce connection pushes.
- Shared gateway protocol v2 requires reloading old v1 owner processes during migration. New activity tools refuse older bridges rather than claiming complete child coverage.

## 0.13.0 — 2026-11-04

- Verify and automatically include new native Git worktree sessions in shared mode, including after adapter reload; use the native project index instead of requiring per-session global grants.
- Separate native API outages, verified project-scope rejection, archived sessions and native-owner absence; do not translate every lookup failure to HTTP 404. Exact-ID verification no longer treats a partial session index as authoritative absence.
- Merge session inventories for several owners of one project and route explicit session IDs to their native API, preferring owners that observed the actual execution events.

- Add a shared multi-project gateway: one loopback port/tunnel routes exact project connections across owning OpenCode processes.
- Discover every active project through authenticated `/v1/projects`, retaining project/session isolation, native subagent trees and existing immutable bindings.
- Keep streams for other projects when one owner closes, and elect a surviving gateway owner after process loss without retrying writes.
- Keep existing project pins in legacy mode; explicit `mode: "shared"` enables migration without globally hardcoded project paths.

## 0.12.1 — 2026-11-04

- Restore completion, question and permission mobile notifications in native TUI owner mode, independently of SSE availability. Delegate server notifications to that owner to prevent duplicate handling.
- Send an informational push after an automatic filesystem Always allow decision; keep manual approvals actionable.
- Recognize native execution success after a missed start or question reply, while deduplicating terminal events.
- Serialize native TUI event processing and label project-path mismatch as “Klasör eşleşmiyor”. This state applies to the owner location and can appear in multiple sessions.

## 0.12.0 — 2026-11-04

- Add read-only interactive session selection through MCP form elicitation, with a structured host-question fallback; return the chosen exact ID without creating a binding until the user choice is connected explicitly.
- Automatically follow the selected root and its verified descendants over SSE, including newly created and nested subagents, without a user-facing scope option.
- Preserve source identity and ancestry through live delivery, replay and client buffer reads; keep unrelated sessions excluded.
- Expose tree member status and active/waiting counts without widening instruction or question targets.
- Add managed MCP capability checks so older bridges cannot silently omit child output.
- Automatically answer native file/directory permissions with Always allow, independently of mobile notification settings, while preserving other approval types and native failure handling.

# OpenCode live control

## Per-chat connections

Version 0.7.0 adds `discover_connections` and `save_connection` to the local MCP
tools. Setup probes only known/default loopback endpoints and protected token
files. It learns project metadata after authentication; returned candidates omit
credentials and token file paths. The selected candidate is revalidated before
saving. Stored profiles contain no session ID. The client may connect by an exact
current main-session title or ID; duplicate titles require explicit selection.
Subagents are hidden unless `includeChildren=true`. Deleted targets are never
retargeted, and the 0.7.0 remote bridge rejects archived sessions as well.

`backeer-codex` 0.4.0 exposes this in chat and through `opencode setup`. It neither
creates SSH tunnels nor accesses Termius vault credentials. If a new computer
has no existing tunnel or protected credential file, setup explains what is
missing. `opencode discover` provides safe diagnostics. New servers need no
extra hosted service. Public packages use `npm run check:package` before publish
to block private configuration files, common credential patterns and fixed real
session IDs from the package's file list.

The 0.6.0 local MCP adapter can manage multiple saved connections. Set
`BACKEER_LIVE_PROFILES_FILE` to an absolute JSON file path:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "connections": [{
    "name": "dev",
    "url": "http://127.0.0.1:43871",
    "tokenFile": "/absolute/private/live-control.token",
    "directory": "/srv/project"
  }]
}
```

Alternatively, `backeer-codex` 0.3.0 configures this file and bundles the local
adapter as a plugin MCP server. No new server is deployed. Profiles hold file
references, never credentials; keep the token in its existing protected file.

Managed tools include `connection_setup`, `diagnose_connection`, `list_connections`, `list_sessions`, `select_session`, `connect_session`,
`session_status`, `send_instruction`, `read_events`, `wait_for_events`, and
`disconnect_session`. Connect with an explicit connection name and existing
session ID. Store the returned `bindingId` only in that chat and pass it to every
subsequent bound tool. There is no global selected session. Bindings are immutable
and each owns an independent session-filtered stream/cursor; even two chats observing the same
session do not consume one another's output. They are local capabilities, not a
multi-user authorization boundary.

The remote bridge must also be 0.6.0 or newer. It exposes its exact project
directory in session metadata and checks the optional `X-Backeer-Project` header
before status, instruction or SSE requests. Managed clients pin that header,
validate exact session identity, and reject changed profiles or wrong projects.
Old single-connection clients remain compatible. No session creation, arbitrary
shell execution or permission bypass is added. Changed credentials require
disconnect/reconnect; no inline token or remote error body is exposed.

Missing profiles allow startup with an empty connection list. There is no imposed profile or active/pending binding quota. Disconnect
unused bindings; remote work continues. Bindings last until this MCP process
ends; reconnect to the same existing session after a restart. Missed history is
not fabricated. Existing gap acknowledgement, request-ID deduplication, heartbeat,
three-second transport reconnection and mobile disconnect/reconnect notices are
unchanged. The manager does not create or supervise the external SSH tunnel.

`connection_setup` is a read-only staged guide: choose a saved connection, or
discover a verified candidate to save, then choose a live main session. It never
selects a target automatically or stores a session ID. `diagnose_connection`
accepts exactly one connection name or binding ID and returns fixed safe messages
for a missing local listener, timeout, credential rejection, project mismatch or
unavailable session. Bound results include stream retry/timing/buffer state.
Temporary transport failures allow reads of already buffered output with
`verified: false`; the immutable binding and cursor survive. New instructions,
answers and gap acknowledgement still require exact target verification after
reconnection. Authentication, project and missing-session errors cannot use the
buffered-read fallback. No POST is automatically replayed.

Windows token files are checked with built-in PowerShell ACL inspection: owner
must be the current user, and allow entries may include only that user, SYSTEM
and Administrators. Broader grants fail closed; paths are never interpolated
into executable script text. Unix uses owner/mode checks as before. Windows ACL
logic has unit coverage; native Windows execution requires a Windows host test.

### Interactive session selection (0.12.0)

After choosing a saved connection, call `select_session` with its connection
name. It fetches a fresh, verified session list and presents main sessions by
default; `includeChildren=true` also exposes child sessions as selectable roots.
This changes the choices shown, not whether connected subagent output is followed.
The optional `message` supplies the selection question in the user's language.

If the MCP host advertises form elicitation, the tool asks through the host's
native selection form. Otherwise it returns `stage: "choose_session"` with the
available `sessions` and exact-ID `options`. The assistant must then use the host's
question interface, or a normal chat question where that interface is unavailable,
and wait for the user's answer. Do not silently pick the first, busiest or most
recent session. Titles are display data; exact IDs disambiguate duplicate titles.
The tool sets no default choice and does not auto-select a single available session.

`select_session` only selects an existing target. It does not create a session,
open an SSE binding, send a prompt or persist a chosen session in the connection
profile. After an accepted user selection, call `connect_session` with the
same connection and selected exact `sessionId`; normal target verification runs
before the binding is created. An accepted native form returns
`stage: "session_selected"`, `sessionId`, `sessionTitle`, and `connected: false`.
A cancelled, declined or timed-out form returns `selection_cancelled`; a target
or profile that changed during selection returns `selection_stale` and requires
a fresh `select_session` call. These outcomes create no binding and leave any
existing binding unchanged. The chosen session and its verified descendants are
then followed automatically, without a second scope question.

The plugin exposes a small, opt-in HTTP bridge **inside the existing OpenCode process**. Output travels over persistent SSE; explicit instructions use authenticated POST requests. The local MCP adapter turns these into tools that Codex can call. No hosted relay, new cloud server, public port, WebSocket service, or terminal OCR is required.

```text
Codex — MCP stdio — local adapter — SSH tunnel — OpenCode plugin
                                 ← SSE events
                                 → POST instruction
```

This channel reports OpenCode sessions, assistant text, selected tool output and status. It is not an arbitrary SSH shell or a byte-for-byte terminal recorder. From 0.12.0 the OpenCode plugin automatically answers native filesystem access prompts with Always allow; other permission approvals use the existing native/Backeer path. The SSE/MCP channel does not grant permissions. From 0.8.0, ordinary questions can also be read and answered by MCP; authentication forms and permission replies are excluded.

### Follow a session and its subagents (0.12.0)

`connect_session` automatically observes the selected session plus its verified
children and nested descendants. No extra option or scope selection is needed.
Listing with `includeChildren=true` only changes the session selection list;
subagent output is followed regardless. The selected root is fixed in each binding.

Managed subscriptions use `/v1/events?sessionID=<selected-root>&scope=tree` and require
the bridge capability `sessionTree`. Unsupported bridges fail explicitly. Both
the remote bridge and the local adapter must be updated; Backeer Codex 0.9.0+
bundles this adapter. Existing profiles and authentication remain unchanged.

The bridge resolves native `parentID` relationships, including agents created
after connection, and retains verified ancestry with replay events. Source
`sessionID` values are preserved; `parentSessionID`, `ancestorSessionIDs` and
`rootSessionID` describe ancestry. A binding may select a subtree, so
`rootSessionID` describes the native tree root, while the binding's `rootSessionId`
is the selected observation target. Only that target and its descendants pass
the live, replay and buffered-read filters. Unrelated sessions and fork provenance
do not expand the scope; project/worktree checks still apply to every member.

`session_status` includes the tree's member states, active/waiting counts and
`failedCount`. A terminal error is reported as `outcome: "failed"` even after the
session becomes idle; the next busy execution clears that previous outcome.
If ancestry cannot be verified, live delivery and replay disclose a
`session_tree_unavailable` gap. A partial status snapshot reports `complete: false`
and `unresolvedCount`; its counts do not establish whole-tree completion. Recover
using the usual status check and explicit gap-cursor acknowledgement.
Treat unknown states as unknown and do not infer whole-task completion from one
agent becoming idle. A child question identifies that child;
instructions still address the selected root only. Ordinary child questions can
use an explicit targetSessionId after fresh ancestry and form verification. Other child control
requires a separate explicit binding. Tree observation does not broadcast writes.

Replay gaps, pagination, bounded buffers and independent chat cursors keep their
existing semantics. No additional SSE connection per agent is required. Native
OpenCode child sessions are supported; agents internal to another process need a
separate adapter. V2 assistant output remains completed, redacted text units,
not raw token deltas.

## Setup

1. Install this version of `backeer-opencode` on the OpenCode host and on the computer running Codex. Enable the bridge using the configuration documented in the package README. It binds only to `127.0.0.1`; the default port is `43871`.
2. Use a **separate random live-control token**, not the mobile ingest token. Keep matching token files on both computers. Files must be regular, owned by the current account and inaccessible to other users (`chmod 600`). Do not put token values in prompts, URLs, shell arguments or MCP configuration. The local adapter reads only the protected file. Token rotation requires restarting the configured plugin and adapter.
3. Forward the port using an existing authorized SSH host configuration:

   ```sh
   while true; do
     ssh -N -T -o BatchMode=yes -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
       -o ConnectTimeout=3 -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \
       -L 127.0.0.1:43871:127.0.0.1:43871 existing-ssh-host
     sleep 3
   done
   ```

   This uses your existing SSH authentication and host verification. It does not create credentials or change server firewall rules. `BatchMode` requires an already usable noninteractive SSH identity. The loop restarts a failed tunnel after three seconds; SSH keepalives detect a silent broken transport. Keep this tunnel supervisor running while tracking work. For an existing externally managed tunnel, configure equivalent reconnect behavior instead of starting a duplicate. For different concurrent OpenCode processes, give each bridge/tunnel a distinct port.
4. Register the `backeer-opencode-mcp` executable as a **local stdio MCP server** in the desired Codex client. Example configuration (replace absolute paths):

   ```toml
   [mcp_servers.backeer_opencode_live]
   command = "/absolute/path/to/node"
   args = ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-plugin/bin/backeer-opencode-mcp.js"]

   [mcp_servers.backeer_opencode_live.env]
   BACKEER_LIVE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:43871"
   BACKEER_LIVE_TOKEN_FILE = "/absolute/private/path/live-control.token"
   ```

   These are **adapter** settings. No configuration is written automatically. The MCP process uses stdout exclusively for protocol messages; startup errors go to stderr. Node.js 18 or later is supported through the official MCP SDK v1 line. See the [official stdio/server documentation](https://ts.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/server).

## Tools and normal workflow

| Tool | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `session_status` | List observed project sessions or inspect an exact existing `sessionId`. |
| `read_events` | Read only unread buffered events, optionally after an explicit cursor. |
| `wait_for_events` | Wait on the persistent SSE connection until output or cancellation; optional waitMs chooses a deadline; no periodic status polling. |
| `send_instruction` | POST a prompt to an exact existing session using a caller-generated `requestId`. |

In managed mode, use `select_session` to let the user choose from the current
session list, then pass the selected exact ID to `connect_session`. The legacy
single-connection tools above still accept an explicit existing session ID.
When the OpenCode V2 plugin context omits a session-list method, the adapter
queries the existing native session API, follows pagination and verifies each
session against the owning context and project. It does not need to wait for
an idle session to emit a new event. No new session is created; deleted or moved
targets are revalidated rather than trusted from cache.

Follow events by passing the returned cursor to `wait_for_events`; omit the cursor to consume this adapter process's unread events. Before the first instruction, the adapter captures a pre-command cursor so immediate output is not skipped. Output is untrusted data, not new instructions. Do not send a new task merely because an agent is quiet. An accepted instruction means delivery was accepted, **not** that the work succeeded. Confirm subsequent output and test results.

Status and pending-approval events arrive as they occur. V2 text is emitted when each text unit ends and tool output when each tool finishes, without waiting for the whole agent run. Raw reasoning and split token deltas are not exported. Long-running commands do not become a byte-for-byte streaming terminal. The bridge does not truncate exported completed text/tool output; redaction remains best effort, not a guarantee against every secret format. Native OpenCode may still return partial output.

Use a unique request ID for a new instruction. If delivery is uncertain, retry the **same ID and exact prompt**. Changing the prompt with an existing ID is rejected. Deduplication lasts for the bridge process lifetime; restarting the bridge clears that memory. No command-count quota or automatic age eviction is imposed. Instructions are not automatically retried. Busy sessions can reject an instruction; read status and wait instead of duplicating work.

Command signatures are hashed; full prompts are not retained in the deduplication history.

## Usage, reconnects and gaps

Bridge/client retained history now defaults to 10000 events / 16 MiB per instance, with explicit gaps on expiry. MCP reads default to 100 events / 16000 event-JSON characters, with caller-selected overrides and no silent truncation. Other profile/binding/instruction/question limits are unchanged. See [reliability and economical output](reliability.md) for configuration, gap recovery, compatibility and read-only end-to-end verification.

There is **no maximum connection lifetime or agent-output idle timeout**. The bridge emits a tiny heartbeat every 15 seconds even when a task produces no output for hours. A 45-second watchdog measures missing **transport traffic**, not missing agent replies. If heartbeats disappear, the client discards the dead socket and reconnects. A caller-selected finite wait or host cancellation ends that tool call and leaves the underlying SSE connection running.

Reload the older single-project listener once when migrating the same port;
it cannot share a port with the new gateway. Keep current remote work intact
and use the owning host's supported plugin reload procedure.

OpenCode may remove `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` from runtime `process.env`. A Linux private server can reuse only its own original password from `/proc/self/environ`; it is neither logged nor copied to configuration. Native API PID, exact-session and project checks still apply. No other PID or port range is inspected.

If both a private stdio server and a shared server load that same project, `liveBridge.owner: "standalone"` restricts the listener to the private server. It detects the current process's existing `--stdio` flag rather than a stored PID or session ID. The shared server's other Backeer duties remain active. The default `owner: "server"` and optional `owner: "tui"` behavior remain unchanged.

Native session lookups share only the same in-flight exact-ID verification. Closing an HTTP reader removes its waiting subscription; it does not cancel another reader or restart the agent. Different session IDs remain independent and have no imposed concurrency quota.

From 0.12.1 the configured TUI owner also runs mobile notification handlers; the server half delegates these events to it. Mobile notifications are independent of live SSE enablement and its project-directory pin. Automatic filesystem replies produce an informational push rather than a pending approval card. A shared owner location can show the same mismatch state in several session tabs; the current session title does not determine the project pin.

### Worktree discovery and accurate session diagnostics (0.13.0)

Shared mode verifies native session locations against the actual Git common
directory, including sessions created directly in a worktree before this adapter
observed them and after reload. Native project-index pagination includes these
sessions without per-ID `sessionWorktrees` configuration. Legacy project mode
retains the original observed-session/explicit-grant rule. A folder name or
matching native project ID without Git verification never grants worktree scope.

Several project owners merge their session inventories. An inventory with
`complete: false` means at least one native API could not be read and is not an
exhaustive list. Exact-ID verification uses the authoritative native lookup even
if the index omits that row. `X-Backeer-Session` keeps metadata/cursors and SSE
routed to the selected session owner. Actual native event observations take
precedence over an API that only knows a persisted row. A changed event source
reconnects with normal explicit replay-gap handling; writes are never retried.

Native transport/authentication/lookup outages produce HTTP 503 with
`native_session_api_unavailable`; they are not converted to missing sessions.
Verified foreign project scope produces HTTP 409 `session_project_mismatch`, an
archived row HTTP 410 `session_archived`, invalid native identity HTTP 502, and
absence in the current native owner HTTP 404 `session_not_found`. The local
adapter reports safe corresponding diagnostics. A 404 from this owner is not
proof of deletion from another process, project or worktree.

## Reliability and direct tools (0.15.0)

- Activity is projected from authenticated SSE, with fresh native reconciliation
  on membership/reconnect/terminal uncertainty and a 30-second periodic check.
  changesOnly:true returns deltas after the first card, without another model.
- Native V2 inbox events provide queued/delivered/cancelled receipts. GET
  /v1/sessions/:session/instructions/:request reads the exact persisted receipt.
  Accepted means admission. Session execution is not per-instruction completion.
- Protected command journals reserve request IDs before admission and preserve
  signatures/receipts across restarts. Prompts/answers/credentials are not stored.
  Interrupted reservations fail closed; no automatic POST replay. Guarantees
  begin with requests recorded by 0.15.0, not historical requests. Do not delete
  journals to repair uncertainty. Shared owners of one verified Git project use
  one journal directory next to their protected registry.
- MCP connection_report separates adapter/embedded/loaded remote versions,
  feature compatibility, owner circuits and latency; unknown checks remain
  unknown. backeer-opencode status displays native RPC state without a model.
  With the TUI entry loaded, /backeer-status or the “Backeer: Bağlantı raporu”
  palette command displays the same local report. keymap registration is owned
  by an app slot so it runs within the native UI context.
- Compatible bindings in one MCP manager share one SSE per authenticated
  endpoint/project; independent cursors, scoped buffers and gap acknowledgement
  remain per binding. Separate MCP processes keep separate transports.
- tail_output, read_errors and tool_result fetch retained source text on demand
  with explicit clipping/expiry. They never consume raw/detail cursors.
- list_questions/answer_question accept an explicit targetSessionId for an
  ordinary descendant form; client and server verify ancestry freshly and pin
  native form revision. Instructions remain root-only. Permission/authentication
  forms are excluded; existing native filesystem auto-allow remains unchanged.
- Health metadata advertises liveProtocol major 1 and optional capabilities.
  Incompatible majors block tracking and commands; missing optional features
  are not inferred from a version string. Old owners must be reloaded for all
  new features; local npm installation does not update remote processes.
- Three consecutive native read failures open a per-owner circuit for ten
  seconds with a single recovery probe. Writes are never retried by this circuit.
  Existing 3/10/30/45-second health/native/aggregate/client budgets remain.

Journals use owner-only directories/files on POSIX and fsync reservations and
immutable transition markers. Unreadable/corrupt reservations remain blocked.
Keep these records when reloading or upgrading the bridge. Receipt lookups are
scoped by project/session/request. A missing receipt is not evidence of no send.
Native V1 transports can expose unknown delivery. Output retention is bounded;
these tools cannot reconstruct expired history or opaque provider-side agents.

# Reliability and economical output

## Read-only end-to-end verification

Use the managed MCP `verify_connection` with a saved connection and exactly one
`sessionTitle` or freshly listed `sessionId`. The Codex CLI equivalent is:

    backeer-codex opencode verify <connection-name> "<exact session title>"

The check authenticates, verifies the exact project, resolves one existing session,
checks that session again, and opens its scoped SSE stream. It sends no prompt,
answers no form, starts no remote service/session, and closes its temporary client.
`timeoutMs` defaults to 5000 (maximum 30000) per network stage. The test proves the
read-only transport chain, not model execution or that future events will arrive.

`checks` separates local runtime, remote installation evidence, remote runtime,
bridge reachability, exact session verification and the SSE handshake. Installation
is confirmed only by a running bridge's valid version; unreachable means unknown,
not uninstalled. Ordinary `session_status` and `diagnose_connection` include these
layers. They do not search remote files or claim a newly installed package has
replaced an older running process.

## Bounded retained history

Bridge and client each default to 10000 events / 16 MiB of serialized retained
payloads. Configure positive integer `BACKEER_LIVE_MAX_EVENTS` and
`BACKEER_LIVE_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES` before starting each process. The remote plugin's
`liveBridge.maxEvents` and `liveBridge.maxBufferBytes` options take precedence.
Limits are per bridge/client, not a total process RSS limit: parsed objects,
transient input buffers, multiple bindings and native libraries use additional
memory. Slow-reader queues use the byte budget too; a full queue disconnects that
reader, whose cursor enables replay or an explicit gap.

Old unread cursors return a gap. Check exact session status and explicitly supply
`gap.cursor` to continue. Oversized events also disclose a gap; oversized SSE
frames block the client with `stream_payload_limit` instead of retrying endlessly.
Increase the budget and reconnect the same selected session when necessary.
Expired output is not persisted to disk or recoverable from this in-memory bridge.
Keep canonical output in OpenCode. Command deduplication is intentionally not evicted:
forgetting request IDs could execute the same work twice. This is not a claim that
all plugin memory is capped.

## Reduce model-context consumption

MCP reads default to 100 events and 16000 event-JSON characters. These are page
budgets, not token counts or hard maxima. Continue with the returned cursor; use
`hasMore` to drain additional pages only when relevant. If one event cannot fit,
`requiredMaxChars` tells the caller the needed budget without advancing past it.
No extra summarization model is invoked and no event text is silently clipped.

Use persistent `wait_for_events` instead of frequent empty reads. Keep independent
binding cursors and send only the next scoped instruction, not the full conversation.
Reuse the same requestId and identical prompt after uncertain delivery. Do not
repeat status/diagnosis while the state is unchanged. These measures reduce repeated
context; they do not guarantee any percentage saving or change provider pricing.

## Compatibility and dependency maintenance

The common-root GitHub workflow tests Node 18/20/22/24 and OpenCode client 2.0.26/2.2.5;
Node 24 runs the development tools. Legacy Node coverage is compatibility testing,
not a recommendation to operate unsupported runtimes. Prefer a maintained LTS.
The workflow runs on changes, manually and weekly after this source is committed
to a GitHub repository with Actions enabled. Adding the YAML locally does not run CI.

ESLint 10 replaces the older tool chain. minimatch is overridden to the patched
11.x API and verified through the real lint configuration. Keep the override until
upstream dependencies adopt a patched release; never use blind audit --force.
Production and full dependency audits are separate checks and fail on moderate+
findings. The shipped OpenCode client stays pinned at 2.0.26; testing 2.2.5 is not
an automatic runtime upgrade.
